Google released a new help document on how to allow Google-Agent to have access to your website. "Google-Agent is the name used by agents hosted on Google infrastructure to navigate the web and perform actions upon user request," the document says.
"Explicitly allowing Google-Agent traffic in your content delivery network (CDN), web application firewall (WAF), or bot-detection service helps prevent legitimate requests from being blocked while preserving your existing security controls," Google added.
Google-Agent is not new, we covered it in March, but this is a new help document on allowing access for Google-Agent.
Google wrote this morning that it "Published a technical guide on how to ensure that Google-Agent has access to your website." This is "to help publishers that want to enable Google-Agent for their website."
The document covers:
- How Google-Agent identifies requests
- Allow traffic in your CDN, Firewall, or bot-detection service
- Troubleshooting
